quarterly_data.signal: CFO Ilan Daskal, FQ4 FY2026 details: operating margin increased 280 basis points from the prior quarter, and a $1.5 million tariffs refund in the quarter slightly benefited it; NSE gross margin 64.1% was 190 basis points higher year-over-year and NSE operating margin beat its 18.2%-19.2% guide 'mainly as a result of higher fall-through'; OSP gross margin 55.2% (up 50 basis points year-over-year). Cash flow from operating activities $66.7 million versus $23.8 million a year earlier; capex $11.1 million in the quarter (versus $5.5 million) and $31.1 million for the full fiscal year (versus $27.8 million). FQ1 FY2027 segment guide: NSE operating margin 23.1% +/- 50 basis points, OSP operating margin 43.2% +/- 20 basis points; tax expense around $12 million; share count around 268 million. CFO on opex: R&D 'It's not going to be materially higher', and 'The leverage kind of will continue to play in favor of the operating margin. Again, yeah, it can continue throughout the fiscal year to, as Oleg mentioned, from the mid to the high 20s.' On the extra week shifting revenue: 'that's not the trajectory that we see for the December quarter.'
quarterly_data.figure: Operating cash flow $66.7M; capex $11.1M (FY $31.1M); FQ1 NSE op margin 23.1%, OSP 43.2%

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Oleg Khaykin on demand and pricing: the data center ecosystem, 'which includes high-performance semis, optical modules, NEMs, and hyperscalers', drove strong demand for lab, production and field instruments; 'The data center ecosystem customer demand for our products remains very strong. We expect continued robust growth in this segment for the next several quarters.' Spirent aside, 'the biggest growth was very much lab and production, followed by aerospace and defense. Lab and production, it's just ticking up double digit revenue growth, in the absolute dollars quarter-over-quarter.' Pricing: 'There's clearly some headwinds on, let's say, the semiconductor pricing', 'but so far we've been just passing all those increases to our customers as part of the price adjustment.' R&D leverage: 'the volumes in lab production are just so much higher than what we've been used to in field instruments. You spend the same R&D, but you get much more margin dollars within a fairly short period of time.' The base service provider business is 'growing 1%, 2%'. Spirent: CFO 'Spirent does grow kind of a single-digit year-over-year', with the first half of the calendar year about 45% of its revenue and the second half 55% (CEO); CFO: 'the savings from the restructuring are being realized'.
quarterly_data.figure: Data-center demand 'very strong', robust growth expected for the next several quarters; lab and production double-digit QoQ growth; semiconductor cost increases passed to customers

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Oleg Khaykin on what drives Viavi's 800G / 1.6T test revenue: '800 Gbps will be a big driver for a long time, because a lot of the data centers are 800 Gbps. Only the new stuff is going to be 1.6 Tbps. There's a big install base that's being upgraded as well'; '1.6 Tbps is really what's the primary lead performance driver today.' 'some of that is going to be substitution against 800 Gbps. What's really going to be driving the growth is the broader and broader adoption of the technology and the volumes of production scaling', and for production test 'you're looking really at the capacity being in place or capacity being replaced, because that's what's ultimately driving your dollars.' He noted the September quarter 'generally for us was a down quarter for NSE', so the guided rise means lab and production and aerospace and defense are more than offsetting the service provider / wireless customers.
